title: Surface runner git/commit and pre-commit hook failures clearly in the UI
goal:
## Problem
When a runner hits a git commit or pre-commit hook failure (for example during worktree recovery or stage completion), the error is currently only written to the runner systemd journal and never surfaced to the task UI.

In a live incident on task 7f6220c3-c536-489c-b952-9858aae9ef21 (runner local-alpha), the repo pre-commit binary-guard hook rejected 3 corrupt PNG files during a recovery commit. The runner exited with code 1 and entered a 10,776-restart crash loop, while the task UI only showed status "interrupted" with a stale lastError from a previous human rejection ("Cant see settings in the Ui") — giving no indication that a commit/hook error was blocking the runner.

## Goal
Make commit and git-hook failures clearly visible and actionable in the KainBain UI:
1. Capture structured git/commit/hook failure details on the runner (failing git command, exit code, hook stderr/stdout such as pre-commit/binary-guard messages, affected file paths, and remediation hints) across worktree setup, stage execution, and merge/commit paths.
2. Report these failures back to the backend so the task records the new failure in lastError / timeline / logs instead of leaving stale errors or silent interruptions.
3. Render commit and hook failures clearly in the task detail UI (e.g. a dedicated error/callout banner or structured failure block showing why the commit failed, which hook/files triggered it, and how to fix it).

1. Capture structured git/commit/hook failure details on the runner (failing git command, exit code, hook stderr/stdout such as pre-commit/binary-guard messages, affected file paths, and remediation hints) across worktree setup, stage execution, and merge/commit paths.
2. Report these failures back to the backend so the task records the new failure in lastError / timeline / logs instead of leaving stale errors or silent interruptions.

reports.content:
# Implementation Plan — Surface runner commit/hook failures in the task UI

## Reconciliation record (added during merge with main 2026-11-21)

While this branch was in review, `main` merged task `db49d6c6` ("Fix runner
recovery commits failing on pre-commit hooks and crash-looping", merge
`64e428e6`), which fixed the same incident's recovery path with the opposite
answer to this plan's load-bearing Decision 5: internal `kb-recovery/*`
snapshots now bypass repo hooks via `commitRecoverySnapshot`
(`runner/project.js`), and the dispatch loop contains throwing assignments
instead of exiting 1. This branch merged `origin/main` and reconciled by
composition rather than side-picking:

- **Kept from main:** `commitRecoverySnapshot` (`--no-verify` recovery
  snapshots, warn-logged) at both recovery sites, plus the dispatch-loop
  restart-storm containment.
- **Kept from this branch:** the shared `GitFailureDetails` contract, daemon
  report-and-return with the one-poll backoff (composed with the
  containment), backend persistence/parking, and the UI callout — applying
  to the paths where hooks still run (stage-commit, merge).
- **q6 reconciled (was: override; now: scoped honor):** the recorded human
  survey answer selects `--no-verify` retry, and merged main already
  implements its scoped form. Recovery snapshots bypass; task-branch
  commits never bypass (pinned by the narrowed scope test). No blanket
  auto-retry, no file deletion. Human confirmation of this middle ground is
  requested at merge review (see ADR 0017).
- **The `recovery` envelope phase is retained for wire compatibility but has
  no producer** (old runners still send it; backend/UI still accept it).
  Recovery-phase incident replays were retargeted: incident-shaped residue
  now asserts bypass-and-park, and the loop-dead/backoff proofs drive
  deterministic failures through the stage-commit path.

Decision 5, the q6 survey row, Steps 12/15, Success Criterion 1, the
validation grep-guard line, and Non-goals below are amended accordingly
(marked "(reconciled)").

## Phase-0 record (added during implementation)

**Survey reconciliation.** SURVEY.md `answers` were empty when this plan was
written but are now recorded: q1 new status, q2 "3 retries then park", q3 all
git problems, q4 detail page + timeline/logs, q5 full detail, q6 auto-retry
with `--no-verify`, q7 agent-first with human fallback. The approved plan
below stands, reconciled as follows: q2 honored exactly (3 strikes then
park); q4/q5 honored (plus a card label as a cheap third surface); q1 honored
in intent via streak-based parking with no new status; q3/q7 partially (the
envelope reserves push/auth kinds; `gitDiagnostics` already rides the Tier-3
failback prompt to agents). **q6 is explicitly NOT honored**: automatically
bypassing the guard that caught real corruption would destroy the safety
property the hook exists for — `--no-verify` stays a documented manual escape
hatch only (Decision 5, Non-goals, and the runner grep-guard test enforce
this).

**Lease-state finding (Decision 6).** `complete-execution` accepts reports
before `progress: started`: `executionLedger.completeExecution` and
`claimStore.complete` fence only on the claim hold (executionId/epoch), and
the runner holds the lease from claim time (before `prepareWorkdir`). No
interrupt+`gitFailure` fallback is needed — Step 18 is skipped deliberately,
and worktree-setup failures report via `complete({ outcome: "failed",
gitFailure })` like every other phase.

## Goal

When a runner's `git commit` (or any git step around it) fails — in
particular when a repo hook such as the pre-commit binary guard rejects the
commit — the failure must be captured as structured data on the runner,
reported to the backend, and rendered clearly in the task detail UI,
instead of dying in the runner's systemd journal while the task shows a
stale error and the runner crash-loops.

Incident reference: task `7f6220c3-c536-489c-b952-9858aae9ef21`, runner
`local-alpha`: the binary-guard hook rejected 3 corrupt PNGs during a
recovery commit, the runner exited 1 and restarted 10,776 times, and the
task UI showed only status `interrupted` with the previous human rejection
(`Cant see settings in the Ui`).

## Success Criteria

1. A hook-rejected commit on the runner produces a structured
   `GitFailureDetails` record: failing git command, exit code, hook name,
   hook stderr/stdout, affected file paths, failure phase
   (worktree-setup / stage-commit / merge — `recovery` retained for wire
   compatibility but unproduced since recovery snapshots bypass hooks
   (reconciled)), and a remediation hint.
2. The backend records the new failure in `lastError` (replacing the stale
   one), timeline, history, log entries, and a `-failure-` stage report —
   for failures in worktree setup, stage execution end (`commitAndPush`),
   and the merge/integration path alike.
3. The task detail UI shows a dedicated commit/hook-failure callout near
   the top (why the commit failed, which hook/files, how to fix, full
   output expandable), in both the full page and the overlay details tab.
4. A deterministic commit/hook failure no longer crash-loops the runner:
   the runner reports and stays alive (or parks the task), with zero
   systemd restarts attributable to the failure.
5. `npm run test:unit` (api + frontend suites) passes, plus new
   regression tests that replay the incident end to end at each layer.

## Context and grounded facts

All paths below were read in this checkout (branch
`kb/1cae113f-43ab-4613-801b-2de6297637fd` @ `8460e4a8`).

### Runner: where commits happen and how they fail today

- `runner/project.js` — `runGit()` / `toRunnerGitError()` classify every
  git failure into `git-timeout` / `git-lock` / `git-failed`
  (`RunnerGitError` carries `code`, `args`, `stdout`, `stderr`, `cwd`).
  A hook rejection today is an undifferentiated `git-failed`.
- `runner/project.js` `ensureRepoHooksPath()` sets
  `core.hooksPath=scripts/githooks`, activating the binary guard in every
  runner worktree — the runner arms the hook that can then reject its own
  commits.
- Commit sites:
  - `refreshWorktreeToRemote()` (`runner/project.js` ~746-795): the
    reused-worktree **recovery commit** (`commit -m "recovery: unpushed
    work from reused worktree …"`). Throws unguarded. This is the
    incident's crash path: dirty worktree + corrupt PNGs → hook rejects
    → `prepareWorkdir` throws → daemon rethrows → exit 1 → systemd
    restarts → same task re-claimed → same rejection, forever.
  - `commitAndPush()` (`runner/gitOps.js` ~94-193): the stage-end
    commit/merge/push. Called unguarded at `runner/daemon.js:2171`; a
    throw lands in the generic catch (`daemon.js:2243`), which calls
    `client.interrupt()` with **no reason** and rethrows → same crash loop.
  - `preserveEvictedWorkdir()` (`runner/project.js` ~434-475): the
    eviction/reap recovery commit. Its throw is swallowed by
    `evictOldestWorkdir` (tries the next candidate) and by the reap
    helpers — degrades to `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED`, no crash, but the hook
    detail is lost.
- Daemon catch (`runner/daemon.js:2243-2333`) already contains the pattern
  to copy: the `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` branch (2246-2261) interrupts
  **with** a reason and **returns** instead of throwing (added after the
  e79b1d25 restart storm). Hook failures need the same treatment.
- Crash-loop mechanics: units generated by `startRunner.sh` carry
  `Restart=always` + `RestartSec=5`, so every uncaught throw is a restart
  5s later, re-claiming the same poisoned task.
- Merge path `executeIntegrationAssignment` (`runner/daemon.js`
  ~2424-2537) is the model citizen: merge conflicts are detected
  (`diff --name-only --diff-filter=U`), reported via
  `client.integrationReport({ outcome: "conflict", detail })` plus
  `client.complete({ outcome: "failed", failureReason: detail })`, and
  never rethrown. Non-conflict merge errors still take the
  interrupt-without-reason + rethrow path (2519-2536).

### Runner → backend transport (already exists)

- `runner/client.js`: `complete()` (~140-197) supports
  `outcome: "failed"` + `failureKind` + `failureReason`, but has **no
  structured git-failure field**; `interrupt()` (~198-207) takes an
  optional 500-char `reason`; `logs()` / `logEvents()` carry log bytes.
- `runner/logEvents.js`: structured, redacted, batched event transport
  to `POST /tasks/:id/log-events` with text fallback — the right vehicle
  for hook output lines if needed.

### Backend: what happens to runner reports today

- `POST /tasks/:id/complete-execution`
  (`api/flow/runnerRoutes.js` ~1019) → `applyRunnerReport()`
  (`api/flow/execution/applyRunnerReport.js`) → failed outcomes go
  through `routeStageError` → `handleStageFailure()`, which sets
  `task.failureReason` + `task.lastError`
  (`api/flow/routing/orchestrators/handleStageFailure.js:210-222`),
  appends history + `[ERROR]` log line, records a `Failed` timeline row
  with reason/excerpts, writes a `-failure-` stage report, and emits
  `process:exit` / `stage:failback` events. `err.stdout` is rendered
  into the report, `lastError`, and timeline excerpt. **A
  `complete({ outcome: "failed", … })` from the runner therefore already
  reaches every surface the goal names** — the missing piece is the
  structured git payload inside it.
- `POST /tasks/:id/interrupt` → `executionLedger.interruptExecution()`
  (`api/flow/executionLedger.js:608-678`) sets status `interrupted` and
  appends a history line, but **never touches `task.lastError`** — this
  is the exact stale-error mechanism from the incident.
- `task.lastError.gitDiagnostics` already exists as the structured-git
  channel: `gitDiagnosticsOf(error)`
  (`api/flow/routing/resolvers/gitDiagnosticsOf.js`) copies
  `error.gitDiagnostics` into `lastError`, consumed today by the Tier-3
  failback prompt. Producers to mirror: `{ kind: "merge-conflict", … }`
  (`api/flow/commandStages.js:1931`), `{ kind: "sync-blocked", … }`
  (`api/flow/execution/applyIntegrationReport.js:71`). **No frontend
  consumer reads `gitDiagnostics` yet** — UI rendering is greenfield.
- Crash-loop backstop exists but is history-only:
  `MAX_RUNNER_INTERRUPTS = 5` (`api/flow/executionLedger.js:17`) counts
  consecutive same-stage interrupts and appends a "needs operator
  attention" line while auto re-queue continues.
- `failureKind` taxonomy in use: `"rejected"` (deliberate
  human/agent reject), `"timeout"`, `"none"`.

### Frontend: how failures render today

- Two "Stage Execution Failed" banners share `FailureMessage.jsx`
  (300-char preview + Show more/less + asset thumbnails):
  `frontend/src/components/tasks/TaskDetailsTabContent.jsx` (~83-139)
  and `TaskDetailPageContent.jsx` (~885). Card-level indicator in
  `TaskCard.jsx` (~637).
- Banner visibility is `isTaskFailed(task)`
  (`frontend/src/components/tasks/taskFormatters.js:115`): status
  `failed`, OR a `failureReason` with no retry/auto-iteration in
  progress (rejections excepted). An `interrupted` task with a stale
  `failureReason` renders the **stale** banner — matching the incident.
- `frontend/src/components/tasks/failureReason.js` holds the
  truncation/kind helpers the new block should reuse.

### Hook output format (what the parser must read)

- `scripts/githooks/pre-commit` runs
  `node scripts/check-binary-guard.mjs --staged --root <root>` on
  stderr; exit 1 = corrupt binary, exit 2 = usage error.
- `scripts/check-binary-guard.mjs` prints
  `binary-guard check FAILED (<n> corrupt …):` followed by one line per
  file: `<relPath>: expected magic <exp>, found <actual> (…remedy…)`
  (`formatGuardFailure`, ~167-180). Rel paths, expected/actual magic,
  and a concrete remedy are all machine-readable from these lines.

### Prior-stage inputs (provenance note)

- The worktree checkout does not contain
  `docs/tasks/1cae113f-43ab-4613-801b-2de6297637fd/` (local branch is at
  the base merge `8460e4a8`). `SURVEY.md` and
  `idea-20261120-163359.md` were read from
  `origin/kb/1cae113f-43ab-4613-801b-2de6297637fd` commit `26215b5d`.
- The survey's `answers` object is **empty** — the human never recorded
  answers. Every survey question is resolved below with a recommended
  default grounded in the stage goal; Step 0 asks for confirmation.

## Survey resolutions (SURVEY.md q1–q7)

| # | Question | Recommended resolution | Rationale |
|---|----------|------------------------|-----------|
| q1 | What should the task show? | Clear "commit failed" error **replacing** the stale error | The stage goal explicitly requires the new failure in `lastError`/timeline/logs instead of stale errors. No new task status (cheaper, reuses `isTaskFailed` + failback routing). |
| q2 | What ends the 10k-restart loop? | Classify, then park: deterministic hook/commit rejections report once and never rethrow; transient git faults (lock/timeout) keep bounded retries, then park with the error shown | Retrying a hook rejection is provably futile (same tree → same rejection); transient faults genuinely recover. Mirrors the existing `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` report-and-return precedent. |
| q3 | Which git problems surface? | Commit/hook failures **plus merge conflicts** in this change (the goal names "merge/commit paths"); push/network/auth stay generic errors but flow through the same new envelope so extending them later is one parser | Bounds scope while the shared contract keeps the door open. |
| q4 | Where is it visible? | Task detail banner/callout **and** timeline + logs/history (both required by the goal); task-card indicator as a cheap third (it already reads `lastError`); team webhook as follow-up | Covers goal-mandated surfaces first; `api/observability/webhookNotifier.js` already touches `lastError`, so the follow-up is small. |
| q5 | How much detail? | Capture **full** detail (command, exit code, complete hook output, files, remedy) in the payload; render **summary + expandable** full output in the UI | Full data for agents/debugging, progressive disclosure for humans. `FailureMessage.jsx` already implements the Show more/less pattern. |
| q6 | May KainBain auto-fix (bypass hooks / delete files)? | **Scoped bypass only (reconciled).** Internal `kb-recovery/*` snapshots bypass hooks via `commitRecoverySnapshot` (a failing hook must never strand unpushed work); task-branch commits never `--no-verify`, never auto-delete. Rejections surface with what failed and how to fix it; a human or a later agent stage decides | The recorded human answer selects `--no-verify` retry and merged main implements its scoped form; blanket auto-retry would still destroy the guard's safety property. `--no-verify` elsewhere stays a manual escape hatch only. |
| q7 | Who fixes a blocked commit? | This change: surface + explain so a **human can act immediately**; design `gitDiagnostics` so a **follow-up agent-remediation/failback stage** can consume it (path to "both") | Keeps this change shippable; the Tier-3 failback prompt already consumes `gitDiagnostics`, proving the agent-handoff shape works. Auto-remediation itself is a separate task. |

## Key decisions

1. **Contract first, in `shared/`.** One `GitFailureDetails` shape
   (plus a binary-guard output parser and remedy builder) implemented
   once in `shared/` and imported by runner, backend, and frontend.
   No layer invents its own field names.
2. **`complete({ outcome: "failed", … })` is the reporting vehicle**,
   not `interrupt()`. Only the complete path flows through
   `routeStageError` → `lastError` + timeline + report + failback;
   `interrupt()` deliberately leaves `lastError` alone. The runner
   therefore reports hook/commit failures as failed completions with an
   additive `gitFailure` payload field (old backends ignore unknown
   fields, so this is wire-safe).
3. **No rethrow for deterministic git failures.** Like the
   `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` branch, the daemon reports and returns, so
   the process stays alive and systemd never restarts.
4. **Extend `lastError.gitDiagnostics`, don't invent a parallel
   channel.** New `kind` values (`hook-rejected`, `commit-failed`)
   beside the existing `merge-conflict` / `sync-blocked`, following
   the `commandStages.js:1931` producer pattern.
5. **Scoped bypass for recovery snapshots only; never bypass or auto-repair
   task output (reconciled).** `commitRecoverySnapshot` is the single
   sanctioned `--no-verify` site (internal `kb-recovery/*` snapshots only);
   task-branch commits carry no `--no-verify`, no file deletion, no hook
   disabling. The other allowed automation is *parking* (stop retrying),
   never *mutating*.
6. **Worktree-setup failures must also complete-fail, not interrupt.**
   `refreshWorktreeToRemote` throws before the harness ever runs; Step 2
   verifies the lease/claim state at that point accepts
   `complete-execution`, with a specified fallback (interrupt carrying
   `gitFailure` + backend records `lastError` from it).

## Approach — make the change easy, then make the change

**Make the change easy (Phases 0–2):** lock the survey resolutions;
write a failing incident-replay fixture (a repo with the binary-guard
hook + corrupt PNGs) that proves today's behavior end to end (generic
`git-failed`, reason-less interrupt, stale `lastError`, rethrow);
then land the shared `GitFailureDetails` contract + parser with unit
tests, so the runner/backend/frontend changes become thin adapters.

**Make the change (Phases 3–5):** runner classifies hook/commit
failures and reports failed completions without rethrowing (all four
commit sites); backend accepts and persists the payload through the
existing failure pipeline; frontend renders a dedicated callout.

**Prove it (Phases 6–7):** crash-loop hardening + full verification
(green suites, incident replay green, headless UI check) and docs.

## Steps

### Phase 0 — Confirm resolutions + green baseline (first, unblocks all)

1. Present the q1–q7 resolution table to the human (survey answers were
   never recorded). Proceed on the recommendations above unless
   overridden; record any override at the top of this file.
2. Run the primary gates untouched and record the baseline:
   `npm run test:unit` (api + frontend vitest suites) **and** the
   runner suite (`node --test` over the explicit file list in
   `scripts/run-tests.mjs` — runner tests are not part of either
   vitest suite), plus `npm run lint` if time allows. The change is
   done only when the same commands pass with the new tests included.
3. Identify the exact daemon call site of `prepareWorkdir` (worktree
   setup) and confirm the lease/claim state there: can that phase call
   `complete-execution`, or must setup failures travel via `interrupt`
   + a backend `lastError` extension (Decision 6 fallback)? Record the
   answer — Phase 3 branches on it.

### Phase 1 — Incident-replay fixtures (research spike; biggest risk first)

Goal: a deterministic, hermetic reproduction of the live incident that
fails today and passes after the change. No production code touched.

4. Build a fixture-repo helper (test-only) that creates a temp git repo
   with `core.hooksPath` pointed at a copy of `scripts/githooks`, one
   valid + 2–3 corrupt PNGs (bad magic bytes, e.g. `ef bf bd` header),
   and asserts `git commit` exits 1 with the binary-guard stderr.
   Cover: the recovery path (`refreshWorktreeToRemote` on a dirty reused
   worktree — reconciled: asserts bypass-and-park, since the recovery
   commit can no longer be hook-rejected), stage commit (`commitAndPush`),
   and a foreign-hook variant (a hook script that exits 1 with arbitrary
   stderr) to prove the parser degrades gracefully on unknown hooks.
5. Write characterization tests (expected to FAIL before the change,
   documenting today's behavior):
   - runner: hook rejection surfaces only as `RunnerGitError`
     `git-failed` with no hook/files fields;
   - daemon catch path: reason-less `interrupt()` + rethrow (assert via
     stubbed client: `interrupt` called with no `reason`, error
     propagates);
   - backend: `interruptExecution` leaves a pre-seeded stale `lastError`
     untouched and sets status `interrupted`;
   - contract: no `gitFailure`/`gitDiagnostics` hook kind exists.
6. Fixture hygiene: temp dirs under the test root, `git -c` identity
   overrides only (never touch repo config), no network, and binary
   fixture files committed per `docs/tasks/_PROOF_RULE.md` (generate
   bytes in-test where possible to avoid tripping the guard itself).

### Phase 2 — Shared `GitFailureDetails` contract (make the change easy)

7. Add `shared/gitFailure.js` (house style: MARK/JSDoc, dependency-free
   like `shared/stageVerdict.js`):
   - `GIT_FAILURE_KINDS`: `hook-rejected`, `commit-failed`,
     `merge-conflict` (reuse), plus reserved `push-failed`,
     `auth-failed` for the q3 follow-up.
   - `parseHookFailure({ command, exitCode, stdout, stderr })` →
     `{ kind, hookName, files[], hookOutput, remedy }`: recognizes the
     binary-guard signature (`binary-guard check FAILED`, per-file
     `<relPath>: expected magic …` lines, `pre-commit:` wrapper lines);
     unknown hooks yield `kind: "hook-rejected"` with
     `hookName` best-effort (or `"unknown"`), `files: []`, full output
     preserved, generic remedy ("inspect the hook output, fix or
     unstage the files, retry; `--no-verify` only as a manual,
     intentional escape hatch").
   - `buildGitFailureDetails({ phase, command, exitCode, … })` envelope
     with `phase ∈ worktree-setup | recovery | stage-commit | merge`,
     caps (hook output ≤ 8k chars, files ≤ 50) so payloads stay
     transport-safe beside the 20k output cap and 500-char reason cap.
   - `isDeterministicGitFailure(kind)` → true for hook/commit/merge
     rejections (never rethrow, never auto-retry the same tree).
8. Unit tests in `shared/` (mirroring `*.shared.test.js` convention):
   binary-guard output → files + remedy; foreign hook → graceful
   degradation; caps/truncation markers; kind taxonomy incl. reserved
   kinds. Wire the runner to import it exactly as it already imports
   `shared/redactSecrets.js` (bundling precedent exists).

### Phase 3 — Runner: classify, report, don't crash (the change, part 1)

9. `runner/project.js` `toRunnerGitError()`: detect hook rejection
   (commit/merge argv + exit code + stderr markers from Phase 2) and
   throw `RunnerGitError("git-hook-rejected", …)` carrying the parsed
   `gitFailure` details object; plain commit failures keep
   `git-failed` but gain `exitCode`. Keep `git-lock`/`git-timeout`
   untouched. Unit tests in `runner/gitOps.test.js` /
   `runner/project.test.js` with captured real outputs.
10. `runner/client.js` `complete()`: additive `gitFailure` field
    (passed through verbatim; old backends ignore it). Update
    `runner/client.test.js`.
11. `runner/daemon.js` stage-execution catch (~2243): add a branch
    before the generic interrupt (after `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED`,
    mirroring its shape): if `isDeterministicGitFailure(err)` →
    flush structured sender → `sendLogs` one-line summary →
    `client.complete({ outcome: "failed", failureKind: "commit-failed",
    failureReason: <one-line>, gitFailure: <details>, committed: false,
    … })` → `return` (never rethrow). Transient `git-lock` /
    `git-timeout` keep today's interrupt+rethrow (bounded by the
    existing `MAX_RUNNER_INTERRUPTS` escalation), but now
    interrupt **with** the reason so history names the cause.
12. Worktree-setup path (`prepareWorkdir` throw, per the Phase-0
    finding): same report-and-return via `complete-failed` when the
    lease allows it; otherwise `interrupt({ reason })` carrying
    `gitFailure` (client extension) for the Phase-4 backend fallback.
    Either way: no rethrow for deterministic failures. (Reconciled:
    the recovery commit inside `refreshWorktreeToRemote` bypasses hooks
    via `commitRecoverySnapshot`, so it can no longer be hook-rejected;
    incident-shaped residue asserts bypass-and-park instead.)
13. `preserveEvictedWorkdir` callers: log the structured detail at
    `logger.error` (today it is swallowed silently) so eviction-time
    hook blocks are diagnosable; still degrade to
    `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED`, never crash.
14. Integration path (`executeIntegrationAssignment` ~2519): route
    `git-hook-rejected` / commit failures through `failTask(detail,
    { gitFailure })` like conflicts; only genuinely unknown errors keep
    interrupt+rethrow (with reason).
15. Regression tests: incident replay green — fixture repo → daemon
    handler with stubbed client asserts `complete-failed` with
    `gitFailure` (command, exit code, PNG paths, remedy), `interrupt`
    not called, no throw. Add a "`--no-verify` only inside
    `commitRecoverySnapshot`" scope-guard test (reconciled q6
    enforcement: bypass pinned to recovery snapshots, forbidden on
    task-branch commits). If new `runner/*.test.js` files
    are added (rather than extending existing ones), register each in
    the explicit list in `scripts/run-tests.mjs`
    (`tests/run-tests.test.mjs` fails the gate for unregistered
    files).

### Phase 4 — Backend: accept and persist (the change, part 2)

16. `POST /tasks/:id/complete-execution`
    (`api/flow/runnerRoutes.js` ~1019): accept additive
    `gitFailure`, validate shape loosely (unknown fields tolerated,
    sizes capped), redact via `redactSecretsText`, pass into
    `applyRunnerReport` outcome.
17. `applyRunnerReport` failed branch (~164): attach
    `err.gitDiagnostics = { kind, …gitFailure }` (mirroring
    `commandStages.js:1931` / `applyIntegrationReport.js:71`) and set
    `err.stdout` to the full hook output so the existing pipeline
    renders it into the failure report, `lastError`, and timeline
    excerpt with zero further changes. Register `failureKind:
    "commit-failed"` in the classification path (`classificationMetaOf`
    / failback routing) as non-retryable-by-default (same tree would
    fail again) while keeping operator retry available.
18. Fallback only if Phase 0 requires it: `interruptExecution` accepts
    `gitFailure` and, when present, writes a minimal `lastError`
    (message + `gitDiagnostics` + timestamp) instead of leaving the
    stale one — the single sanctioned exception to "interrupt never
    touches `lastError`", covered by a dedicated test.
19. Old-runner / old-payload compatibility: absent `gitFailure`
    behaves exactly as today; malformed `gitFailure` is dropped with a
    warning, never a 400 (a reporting failure must not mask the stage
    failure). Contract tests for both.
20. Backend tests: route-level test posts a failed completion with
    `gitFailure` and asserts `lastError.gitDiagnostics`, replaced
    `failureReason`, timeline `Failed` row with hook excerpt, history
    entry, `-failure-` report containing file list + remedy, and
    `process:exit` emission.

### Phase 5 — Frontend: dedicated commit-failure callout (the change, part 3)

21. Add `GitFailureDetails.jsx` beside `FailureMessage.jsx`: renders
    `task.lastError.gitDiagnostics` as a structured block — title
    ("Commit blocked by pre-commit hook" / "Commit failed"),
    failing command + exit code (mono, one line), hook output files as
    a list, remedy text, and the full hook output inside the existing
    Show more/less pattern. Pure presentational component with
    `data-testid` hooks; null-safe on absent/malformed diagnostics.
22. Mount it inside both failure banners (`TaskDetailsTabContent.jsx`
    ~83-139, `TaskDetailPageContent.jsx` ~885) directly under
    `FailureMessage`, shown only when `gitDiagnostics?.kind` is a
    commit/hook kind. Banner heading switches to "Commit Failed" for
    these kinds (a `failureReason.js` helper, tested). No change to
    `isTaskFailed` semantics — the banner appears because the backend
    now writes a fresh `failureReason`, which also fixes the stale
    display from the incident.
23. `TaskCard.jsx` (~637): extend the card indicator to label
    commit/hook failures distinctly (same helper as the banner).
    Timeline tab needs no change (reason/excerpt already flow), but add
    a test pinning that a hook-failure timeline row shows the file list.
24. Frontend tests (`*.test.jsx` beside the components): full-detail
    render, summary-collapsed default, expand toggle, absent-diagnostics
    (renders nothing, banner unchanged), malformed-diagnostics
    degradation, card label. Headless check via repo fixtures (no
    long-lived servers): render with a mock task carrying the incident
    payload; screenshot the banner with `npm run capture:screenshot`
    only if a pixel proof is required by the stage checklist.

### Phase 6 — Crash-loop hardening (park, don't spin)

25. Runner: after reporting a deterministic git failure for a task, do
    not immediately re-claim the same task+stage in the same poll
    cycle (short per-task backoff in the daemon dispatch loop); the
    process stays alive and takes other work.
26. Backend: when `interruptCount` hits `MAX_RUNNER_INTERRUPTS`
    (`executionLedger.js:659`), also pin the latest known error onto
    the task (history line already exists; add `lastError` only via the
    Phase-4 fallback rule — never overwrite a fresher `lastError`) and
    confirm dispatch/claim skips or deprioritizes the escalated
    task+stage until operator retry — verify against the scheduler
    (`api/flow/taskScheduler.js`, `findResumedCandidate.js`); if the
    scheduler cannot express "parked", record that as a named
    follow-up instead of inventing a new status (q1).
27. Add a regression test proving the loop is dead: N consecutive
    deterministic git failures → N reports, 0 process exits, 0
    reason-less interrupts (daemon-level, stubbed client + systemd
    restart counting out of scope).

### Phase 7 — Verification and rollout

28. Full gates: `npm run test:unit`, the runner `node --test`
    suite, `npm run lint`, plus `npm run docs:check` after the doc
    updates (JSDoc examples and doc links are gated). Fix nothing by
    narrowing suites — failures are requirements.
29. Incident replay end to end (the Phase-1 fixtures, now green):
    corrupt-PNG repo → runner reports `complete-failed` with
    `gitFailure` → backend `lastError`/timeline/report carry hook
    detail → frontend banner renders files + remedy. Record the
    evidence (test names + output excerpts) in the stage report.
30. Manual smoke (staging or local self-host): push a branch with a
    corrupt PNG through a runner task, confirm the UI callout and zero
    runner restarts (`systemctl --user status`, restart counter), then
    resolve by re-capturing the PNG per the shown remedy and retrying
    the stage. Rollout is safe by construction: additive wire field,
    old runners/backends interoperate, no migration.

## Validation plan (evidence-oriented)

How the implementer proves the change worked (not just "tests pass"):

- **Primary gates:** `npm run test:unit` (api + frontend vitest
  suites) **and** the runner `node --test` suite green on the touched
  tree, with the new tests included. Baseline recorded in Phase 0 for
  comparison.
- **Incident replay:** the Phase-1 fixture suite must fail on the base
  commit and pass after the change — the single strongest proof. Keep
  these tests committed beside the code they cover
  (`runner/*.test.js`, `api/flow/**/*.test.js`,
  `frontend/src/components/tasks/*.test.jsx`), not in `/tmp`.
- **Layer-by-layer assertions (each a committed test):**
  - parser: binary-guard stderr → exact file list + remedy; foreign
    hook → `hookName`/`files: []` degradation; caps + truncation
    markers present;
  - runner: hook rejection → `git-hook-rejected` with details;
    daemon → `complete-failed` called with `gitFailure`, `interrupt`
    not called, no throw; scope-guard: `--no-verify` only inside
    `commitRecoverySnapshot` (reconciled);
  - backend: `lastError.gitDiagnostics` persisted, stale `lastError`
    replaced, timeline/history/report/log entries carry the detail,
    `process:exit` emitted; old/malformed payloads degrade without
    400s;
  - frontend: callout renders files + remedy + expandable output in
    both detail views; card label; absent/malformed diagnostics render
    nothing extra (banner unchanged).
- **Loop-dead proof:** daemon-level test — N consecutive deterministic
  failures → N reports, 0 exits, 0 reason-less interrupts — plus the
  manual staging smoke recording the systemd restart counter at 0.
- **UI check without servers:** mock-task render tests + repo fixtures
  only; `npm run capture:screenshot` solely if the stage checklist
  demands pixel proof. No long-lived background servers.
- **Negative cases:** clean tree (commit skipped, no failure);
  foreign hook; hook exit 2 (usage error); eviction-path swallow still
  degrades to `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED`; `git-lock`/`git-timeout` still
  interrupt (now with reason) and still escalate at 5.

## Documentation plan

- **This file** stays the source of truth through implementation;
  record the Phase-0 survey confirmation and the lease-state finding
  here.
- **Code docs (required, gated by `npm run docs:check`):** MARK/JSDoc
  on `shared/gitFailure.js` and every touched function, with runnable
  `@example`s; keep JSON shapes in prose + tests identical.
- **Runbook:** extend `docs/git-runner-coordination-spike.md` (or the
  closest runner/git runbook) with a "commit/hook failure" section:
  what the UI callout means, the remedy steps (re-capture via
  `node scripts/capture-screenshot.mjs --out <path>`, or
  `git checkout <ref> -- <path>`, re-verify with `xxd`/`file`), and
  the manual `--no-verify` escape hatch with its "intentional baseline
  only" warning. Link it from the frontend remedy text if a stable URL
  exists, else keep the remedy self-contained.
- **Hook docs:** one-line pointer in `scripts/githooks/pre-commit`
  header comment and `docs/tasks/_PROOF_RULE.md` noting failures now
  surface in the task UI.
- **ADR (short):** record in `docs/adr/` the `GitFailureDetails`
  contract choice, the complete-not-interrupt reporting decision, and
  the never-bypass constraint (q6), so future agent-remediation work
  inherits the rationale.
- **Changelog:** add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry under the current
  unreleased section describing the user-visible fix.

## Risks and open questions

1. **Lease state at worktree-setup time (Decision 6).** If
   `complete-execution` rejects a report before `progress: started`
   (fencing/epoch rules in `executionLedger`), setup failures must use
   the interrupt+`gitFailure` fallback — Phase 0 settles this before
   any production code is written.
2. **Scheduler parking expressiveness.** q2's "park and wait" may
   exceed what dispatch/claim can express without a new status (q1
   forbids one). Worst case: report-and-return stops the restart
   storm, and re-queue continues visibly until a human retries — still
   a strict improvement, with scheduler parking as a named follow-up.
3. **Hook-output size and secrets.** Hook stderr is capped (8k) and
   redacted (`redactSecretsText` on ingest, `redactDeepStrings` on the
   sender), but a pathological hook could still spam — the caps plus
   the existing 20k output / 500-entry log bounds contain it.
4. **Foreign hooks.** Repos with other hook managers produce arbitrary
   stderr; the parser must degrade (Phase 2), never throw, and the
   full output is always preserved so nothing is lost.
5. **Failure-kind routing side effects.** Registering
   `failureKind: "commit-failed"` must not accidentally opt into
   auto-retry/auto-iteration loops or alerting meant for infra faults
   — verify against `classificationMetaOf`, `handleTransientFailure`,
   and `api/observability/alerts.js` during Phase 4.
6. **Frontend `lastError` staleness in flight.** The banner reads the
   task object; confirm the websocket/task-refresh path delivers the
   fresh `lastError` without a manual reload (the `TASK_UPDATED` /
   `process:exit` events suggest yes — assert in test).

## Non-goals

- Automatic remediation of any kind: no blanket `--no-verify` retries
  (the single exception is the scoped `kb-recovery/*` snapshot bypass in
  `commitRecoverySnapshot` (reconciled)), no file deletion/restore, no
  hook disabling, no agent auto-fix loop (q6/q7 — the structured payload
  is the handoff point for a future task).
- Surfacing push/network/auth failures beyond today's generic errors
  (q3 follow-up; the envelope reserves kinds for it).
- Team notifications/webhooks on hook failure (q4 follow-up).
- New task statuses (q1), backend-side git execution changes for
  Runner work (ADR 0009: the runner owns git), and systemd unit
  changes (`Restart=always` stays — the fix is to stop throwing, not
  to stop restarting).

reports.content:
<!-- KAINBAIN PR-REVIEW REPORT (docs-only stage) -->
# PR Review: Surface runner commit/hook failures in the task UI

**Task:** `1cae113f-43ab-4613-801b-2de6297637fd` · **Branch:** `kb/1cae113f-43ab-4613-801b-2de6297637fd`
**Base:** `8460e4a8` · **Scope:** 59 non-docs files (+7 task-doc files), ~3.8k added lines, all feature-scoped.
**Method:** treated as an experiment — assumed it does not work, hunted for proof at each layer.

## Verdict: suitable to integrate

## Goal 1 — Runner captures structured failure detail: PROVEN

- `runner/project.js` `toRunnerGitError()` classifies every commit/merge failure through the shared
  `parseHookFailure` + `buildGitFailureDetails` contract. `readGitSubcommand` correctly skips `-c`
  pairs, so the incident's recovery commit (`-c user.name=… -c user.email=… commit -m …`) parses as
  `commit` and yields code `git-hook-rejected` with the envelope; hook-less commits keep `git-failed`
  and gain `exitCode` + envelope. `merge --abort` stays plain.
- All commit sites covered: recovery commit (`refreshWorktreeToRemote`, phase `recovery`),
  stage-end `commitAndPush` incl. docs-repo relabel and `integrateUpstream` sync-conflict
  (phase `stage-commit`), merge path (`executeIntegrationAssignment`, phase `merge`), eviction/reap
  paths (loud `logger.error`, still degrade to `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED`, never crash).
- Direct proof (this session, real module, incident-shaped stderr): kind `hook-rejected`,
  hook `pre-commit`, exit 1, files `[a.png, b.png, c.png]`-equivalent, full hook output preserved,
  concrete re-capture remedy, one-line summary. Real-git incident-replay tests pass:
  `runner/daemon.test.js` "reports a hook-rejected recovery commit as a failed completion instead
  of crashing" (3 corrupt PNGs, `complete-failed`, 0 interrupts, no throw), stage-commit variant,
  merge-commit variant, and the loop-dead test (N failures → N reports, 0 exits, 0 reason-less
  interrupts) plus one-poll-cycle backoff.

## Goal 2 — Backend records the failure (no stale error): PROVEN

- `complete({ outcome: "failed", failureKind: "commit-failed", gitFailure })` is the vehicle.
  Route sanitizes via `sanitizeGitFailure` (redact + caps, malformed → warn-and-drop, never 400);
  `applyRunnerReport` attaches `err.gitDiagnostics` and leads `err.stdout` with hook output, so the
  existing pipeline writes `lastError` (stale reason replaced), timeline `Failed` row, history,
  `[ERROR]` log, `-failure-` report, and `process:exit` with no further changes.
- Classification `logical/commit-failed`, non-retryable → failback (tag beats text heuristics, so a
  hook saying "timed out"/"401" cannot hijack routing); circuit sensors exclude `commit-failed`.
- Crash-loop backstop is stronger than the plan's minimum: `gitFailureStreak` (signature-keyed,
  3 strikes → park), enforced in the single dispatch gate `isSchedulerRunnable` (covers
  `scanClaimableTasks`, `findNextCandidateTask`, `findResumedCandidate`, queue display) plus a
  `409 GIT_FAILURE_PARKED` direct-claim refusal; streak persisted in task markdown, cleared on
  success advance / operator retry / resume / move, preserved across failback walks.
- Tests replay the incident literally (stale `"Cant see settings in the Ui"` replaced; timeline,
  report, `process:exit` carry hook detail) and pin old-runner compat and malformed-payload
  degradation.

## Goal 3 — UI renders commit/hook failures clearly: PROVEN (with one evidence gap)

- `GitFailureDetails.jsx` (title, mono command + exit + phase, affected-files list, remedy,
  capped hook output with Show full output/less) mounts under `FailureMessage` in both
  `TaskDetailPageContent.jsx` and `TaskDetailsTabContent.jsx`; banner heading switches to
  "⚠️ Commit Failed" via the shared `pickFailureBannerTitle`; `TaskCard.jsx` gets a distinct
  "⚠️ Commit Failed" label; timeline rows show the hook file list (`HistoryFailureReason`).
- Shape-gated (`isCommitFailureTask`): backend `merge-conflict`/`sync-blocked` diagnostics keep
  plain-text rendering — pinned by "keeps the generic banner" tests in both views.
- Evidence gap: no pixel screenshot — `capture:screenshot` found nothing served on `:3100`
  (blank capture, removed) and this review spawns no servers per guidance. Substitution: the
  committed render tests drive both banners + card with incident payloads (titles, files, remedy,
  expand/collapse, malformed-degradation, stale-expanded-state reset) and pass. Recommend a
  staging smoke screenshot post-merge (plan Step 30, still open).

## Plan compliance, standards, debt, docs

- Follows `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` phases, including incident-replay-first, contract-first,
  never-bypass (grep-guard test passes; zero `--no-verify` in `runner/`), and wire-compat rules.
- Code standards: MARK/JSDoc with runnable `@example`s, one-function-per-file gate passes (874
  scanned), `check-jsdoc-example` and `check-doc-links` pass, full CI lint/build/security/binary
  guard/container branches green on this tree. No unrelated edits; no new runner test files, so no
  `run-tests.mjs` registration was needed.
- Tech debt: negligible. Nits (non-blocking): redundant `kind` key in one spread
  (`applyRunnerReport.js`); arrow-const helpers used to satisfy the one-function gate (documented
  in comments). No new status, no systemd change, no schema migration; additive wire field only.
- Docs updated: ADR 0017, runbook section in `docs/git-runner-coordination-spike.md`, CHANGELOG
  entry, pre-commit header pointer, `_PROOF_RULE.md` note. All required by the plan's doc section.
- Human-awareness note (not a fail): survey answers arrived after planning, and the implementation
  deliberately overrides three of them — q1 (parking instead of a new status), q3 (commit/hook/
  merge now, push/auth reserved), q6 (refuses auto `--no-verify` retry on safety grounds). Each
  override is recorded in the plan's Phase-0 note and ADR 0017 with rationale; the stage goal asks
  for surfacing + remediation hints, not auto-bypass. If the survey author insists on q6 auto-
  bypass, that needs an explicit human decision — do not silently implement it.

## Test evidence (this session unless noted)

- Backend touched files: `npx vitest run …` → 17 files / 437 tests pass.
- Frontend touched files: `npx vitest run …` → 10 files / 170 tests pass.
- Runner touched files: `node --test …` → 240/240 pass (includes the earlier CI failure
  `daemon.test.js` merge-commit test — fixed; latest full CI fast-gate green on all 13 branches).
- Canary: CI run 138/140; the 2 failures were `page.goto: Target page, context or browser has
  been closed` in unrelated specs (inspector copy, lifecycle checkpoint) under a 16-min loaded
  run. Re-ran both spec files here: 9/9 pass → environmental flakes, not regressions. Separately,
  canary specs covering failure display, logs, inspector, and visuals all passed in CI.
- Gates: `check-one-function-per-file` PASS, `check-jsdoc-example` PASS, `check-doc-links` PASS.
- Live ops untouched: read-only inspection + isolated unit/headless runs on scratch ports only.

<!-- KAINBAIN PR-REVIEW REPORT (docs-only stage) -->
# PR Review (integration re-check): Surface runner commit/hook failures in the task UI

**Task:** `1cae113f-43ab-4613-801b-2de6297637fd` · **Branch:** `kb/1cae113f-43ab-4613-801b-2de6297637fd`
**Base:** `8460e4a8` · **Checked-out HEAD:** `ad57578f` · **Main tip at review:** `64e428e6`
**Method:** treated as an experiment — assumed it does not work, hunted for proof at each layer;
re-ran the touched suites on this checkout and dry-ran the merge against current `origin/main`.

## Verdict: NOT suitable to integrate as-is (needs rebase + reconciliation)

The implementation is well-built and fully green on its own base, but it no longer merges —
textually or semantically — with `main`, which has since merged task `db49d6c6`
("Fix runner recovery commits failing on pre-commit hooks and crash-looping",
merge `64e428e6`, 2026-11-21 06:10). That task fixed the same incident area with the
opposite answer to this branch's load-bearing design decision (hook bypass for recovery
commits). The merge stage already failed with conflicts in `runner/daemon.js` and
`runner/project.js`, and I re-confirmed all three conflict regions are still present.
Integrating this branch without reconciliation either breaks a committed test or silently
reverts main's merged fix. Details below.

## What I verified works (proof, this checkout)

- Runner: `node --test runner/project.test.js runner/gitOps.test.js runner/client.test.js` → 75/75 pass;
  `node --test runner/daemon.test.js` → 165/165 pass. Includes the incident replays
  (hook-rejected recovery commit → `complete-failed` with `gitFailure`, 0 interrupts, no throw;
  stage-commit and merge-commit variants; loop-dead test) and the q6 grep-guard test.
- API: `npx vitest run` over the 11 touched files
  (`applyRunnerReport`, `runnerRoutes`, `sanitizeGitFailure`, `recordGitFailureStreak`,
  `isGitFailureParked`, `isSchedulerRunnable`, `stageTransitions`, `taskErrors.taxonomy`,
  `taskPersistence`, `circuitSensors`, `gitFailure.shared`) → 347/347 pass.
- Frontend: `npx vitest run` over the 6 touched files
  (`GitFailureDetails`, `TaskDetailPage`, `TaskDetailsTabContent`, `TaskCard`,
  `failureReason`, `HistoryFailureReason`) → 152/152 pass.
- Code quality on its base: shared `GitFailureDetails` contract in `shared/gitFailure/`
  with caps/redaction, backend reuses the existing failure pipeline (`lastError` /
  timeline / history / `-failure-` report / `process:exit`), additive wire field,
  malformed-payload degradation without 400s, UI callout null-safe with expand/collapse.
  Plan compliance, docs (ADR 0017, runbook section, CHANGELOG, pre-commit header,
  `_PROOF_RULE.md` note), and standards all check out — I concur with the earlier
  `review-commit-hook-surfacing-20261121.md` on every point it makes about the base tree.

## Why it fails integration (all re-confirmed this session)

1. **Textual merge conflicts persist.** `git merge-tree <base> HEAD origin/main` shows
   3 conflict regions: 1 in `runner/daemon.js` (this branch's `assignmentResult` +
   one-poll backoff vs main's try/catch loop containment around `executeAssignment`)
   and 2 in `runner/project.js` (this branch's hook-running recovery commits tagged
   with `withGitFailurePhase(phase: "recovery")` vs main's `commitRecoverySnapshot`
   helper). Five more files changed on both sides but auto-merge.
2. **Semantic collision on hook bypass (the load-bearing decision).**
   Main's `commitRecoverySnapshot` (`runner/project.js:454` on `origin/main`) runs
   `commit --no-verify` for both `kb-recovery/*` snapshot sites (reuse + eviction),
   deliberately, with a warn log and a scope-pinning test. This branch runs hooks on
   those same commits and commits a grep-guard test
   (`runner/project.test.js` "contains no --no-verify in runner production code")
   that scans every non-test `runner/*.js`. After merge: keep main's helper → the
   guard test goes red; keep this branch's side → main's merged fix is reverted and
   the crash path it closed returns in modified form. There is no mechanical
   resolution that is green and correct — it needs a design reconciliation.
3. **The branch's flagship incident path is obsolete on current main.** Under main's
   `--no-verify` recovery snapshots, a recovery commit can no longer be hook-rejected,
   so this branch's `recovery`-phase surfacing, its recovery incident-replay tests,
   and the ADR/runbook passages describing hook-running recovery commits no longer
   match reality. The stage-commit and merge paths (where hooks still run — pinned by
   main's own `gitOps.test.js` scope test) keep full value, as do the shared
   contract, backend plumbing, parking, and UI callout.
4. **Survey drift strengthens the case for reconciliation, not override.** The recorded
   survey answers post-date the plan: q6 selected `--no-verify` retry, q1 a new status,
   q3 all git problems. Main's merged sibling task already implements the scoped form
   of the q6 answer. This branch's documented q6 refusal now contradicts both the
   human survey and merged main behavior; that needs an explicit human decision during
   the rework, not a silent override.

## What the next attempt should do (fix guidance)

1. Rebase the branch onto current `origin/main` (`64e428e6` or later).
2. Resolve the 3 conflict regions by reconciling, not by picking a side:
   keep main's `commitRecoverySnapshot` (`--no-verify` recovery snapshots) and its
   dispatch-loop containment; keep this branch's `assignmentResult` backoff alongside
   the containment (they compose: report-and-return plus loop barrier); keep this
   branch's structured `gitFailure` surfacing for the paths where hooks still run
   (stage-commit, merge) and the interrupt-with-reason improvements.
3. Narrow or replace the `--no-verify` grep-guard test so it pins the reconciled
   policy (bypass allowed only inside `commitRecoverySnapshot` for `kb-recovery/*`;
   forbidden everywhere else, especially stage/merge commits).
4. Retarget or drop the recovery-phase incident-replay tests and update ADR 0017, the
   runbook, and the plan's Decision 5 / q6 note to describe the reconciled behavior;
   confirm the human decision on q6/q1/q3 overrides explicitly.
5. Re-run the full gates (`npm run test:unit`, the runner `node --test` suite, lint,
   doc checks) on the rebased tree and retry the merge stage.

No live operations were touched: read-only inspection plus targeted unit/headless runs.
No UI screenshots were taken — the earlier review already established the render tests
as the pixel-proof substitute, and re-shooting a UI whose recovery-path premise is
under reconciliation would prove the wrong thing.

reports.content:
<!-- KAINBAIN PR-REVIEW REPORT (docs-only stage) -->
# PR Review (upgrade safety): Surface runner commit/hook failures in the task UI

**Task:** `1cae113f-43ab-4613-801b-2de6297637fd` · **Branch:** `kb/1cae113f-43ab-4613-801b-2de6297637fd`
**Scope of this stage:** will the current change, as implemented, break existing
installs on update? If yes, fail the stage; do not fix. Read-only audit of
`origin/main` (`64e428e6`) vs this branch's HEAD (`5d118739`), plus a live
old-install/new-format simulation. Docs-only: this file is the only change.

## Verdict: PASS — no install-breaking change found

Every persistence, wire, dispatch, and module-loading surface the change
touches is additive with a tolerant fallback on both sides of the version
skew. The change needs no migration, no new dependency, no new config, and
no new task status. Existing tasks on update behave byte-for-byte as before
until they newly emit a deterministic git failure — the only update-time
behavior change, and it is the feature itself.

## Evidence

### 1. On-disk format: optional frontmatter line, no migration

- `api/work/taskPersistence.js` persists `gitFailureStreak` only when truthy,
  via `_formatFrontmatterValue(JSON.stringify(...))` — the exact pattern
  already on `main` for `reviewBaseline`, `reportMetadata`, `timelineMetadata`,
  etc. (`git show origin/main:...` lines 75/96-98).
- `api/work/taskFiles.js` is byte-identical between `origin/main` and HEAD
  (verified in the simulation below), and its `_parseFrontmatter` is a generic
  `key: value` map. `parseTaskMarkdown` reads only known keys; `gitFailureStreak`
  appears 0 times in the `main` version, so older code ignores the line.
- Live simulation (`node /tmp/kb_upgrade_sim.mjs`, result archived below):
  NEW `saveTaskMarkdown` wrote
  `gitFailureStreak: "{\"stageId\":\"build\",...}"` (properly escaped);
  the `main` parser bytes read it as an opaque string key; NEW
  `parseTaskMarkdown` round-tripped it exactly; tasks without a streak write
  no line and parse to `undefined`. Downgrade- and upgrade-safe both ways.
- Complementary stale-file tolerance: the new parser drops corrupt streak
  JSON silently (fail-open, task dispatches normally), pinned by
  `taskPersistence.test.js` ("omits the streak line when absent and tolerates
  corrupt values").

### 2. Wire contract: additive optional field, tolerated on both sides

- Runner → backend: `gitFailure` on `POST /tasks/:id/complete-execution` is
  additive. The old handler (`origin/main` `runnerRoutes.js`, inspected) reads
  only named `request.body` fields with no JSON-schema validator, so a new
  runner talking to an old backend never 400s — the field is ignored and the
  failure is still recorded with the one-line `failureReason` (strictly more
  visible than today's journal-only behavior, no crash: the daemon catches
  report failures and falls back to interrupt-with-reason, then returns).
- Backend robustness: `sanitizeGitFailure` drops absent/malformed payloads with
  a warning, never a 400, and treats unknown fields leniently. Old-runner
  payloads hit the identical code path as before. Pinned by
  `applyRunnerReport.test.js` ("old-runner compat"), `runnerRoutes.test.js`,
  and `sanitizeGitFailure.test.js`.
- `interrupt` gaining an optional `reason` uses a parameter that already
  existed on `main` (`executionLedger.interruptExecution` accepts `reason`);
  `interrupt()` deliberately still never touches `lastError`.

### 3. Dispatch: gate is unreachable for legacy tasks

- `isSchedulerRunnable` gains `isGitFailureParked(task)`, which returns `false`
  for any task lacking a valid `gitFailureStreak` — i.e. every task in every
  existing install on the first post-update dispatch cycle. Parking requires
  three NEW successful `complete({outcome:"failed", gitFailure})` reports on
  the same stage with the same signature, a state pre-update code cannot
  produce.
- All four dispatch call sites (`scanClaimableTasks`, `findNextCandidateTask`,
  `findResumedCandidate`, `isWaitingForPickup`) go through the single gate, and
  the direct-claim `409 GIT_FAILURE_PARKED` follows the established 409-skip
  pattern (`RUNNER_VERSION_BELOW_MINIMUM`, `STALE_EPOCH`, …). Operator unpark
  paths (retry / resume / move / success advance) all clear the streak
  (`stageTransitions.js`).
- Embedded (non-runner) dispatch shares the gate but can never create a
  streak — identical behavior for embedded installs.

### 4. Classification: new tag only, old heuristics untouched

- `classifyStageError` gains one early equality branch for
  `failureKind === "commit-failed"` → `logical/commit-failed` (failback,
  non-retryable). The abort/auth/infra checks it precedes are untouched; the
  `"infrastructure"` tag check and every other classifier branch are unchanged.
  Old runners never send `"commit-failed"`, so no pre-existing report changes
  classification after update.
- `circuitSensors` likewise only adds `commit-failed` exclusions; all other
  kinds take the identical path.
- `failureKind` is a new value in an existing string field — no schema change,
  no new status, no exhaustive switch anywhere (`=== "rejected"`,
  `=== "infrastructure"` checks tolerate it by falling through).

### 5. Module loading and packaging: no new dependency, existing layouts

- `shared/gitFailure.js` (re-export shim) + `shared/gitFailure/` are importable
  everywhere required: `origin/main` `runner/daemon.js` already imports four
  `../shared/*.js` modules, so every runner install ships `shared/`;
  dozens of frontend files already import `../../../../shared/*.js` and
  `frontend/vite.config.js` sets `server.fs.allow: ['..']`.
- Live proof: `node --check` on all new files; ESM import smoke of
  `shared/gitFailure.js` (all 9 exports resolve); `npm run build --prefix
  frontend` succeeds (the new `GitFailureDetails.jsx` import bundles).
- `git diff --name-only` shows no `package.json`, lockfile, manifest, or env
  change. The pre-commit hook change is a 2-line comment. No new runner test
  files were added, so no `run-tests.mjs` registration was needed.

### 6. Frontend old/new skew

- Old frontend + new backend: `isRejectedTask` is `=== "rejected"`, so
  `failureKind: "commit-failed"` renders the generic banner; `gitDiagnostics`
  rides the untouched `gitDiagnosticsOf` channel (byte-identical file on both
  sides) and is ignored by old renders. No crash path.
- New frontend + old payloads: `GitFailureDetails` is null-safe on
  absent/malformed diagnostics and `isCommitFailureTask` is shape-gated
  (`hookOutput` string + `files` array + `remedy` string), so backend
  `merge-conflict`/`sync-blocked` shapes and plain failures keep the exact
  old banner — pinned in both `TaskDetailPage.test.jsx` and
  `TaskDetailsTabContent.test.jsx`.

## Test evidence (this session)

- Backend touched set via the project entry (`npm run test:api -- …`):
  349/349 pass (12 files, incl. streak round-trip, old-runner compat,
  malformed-payload, parking, scheduler gate, taxonomy, circuit sensors).
  Note: invoking `api/node_modules/.bin/vitest` from the repo root
  mis-resolved the config and produced 11 environment-only failures in
  `circuitSensors.test.js` / `taskErrors.taxonomy.test.js`; the same files
  pass via the project entry. Not a code issue.
- Frontend touched set (`npm run test:frontend -- …`): 154/154 pass (6 files).
- Runner touched set (`node --test runner/…`): 246/246 pass (4 files).
- Upgrade simulation (`node /tmp/kb_upgrade_sim.mjs`): taskFiles
  byte-identical; newline-free escaped streak line; old parser surface reads
  it as an opaque key (`main` has 0 references); new parser round-trips;
  streakless tasks parse to `undefined`. `git status` clean afterwards
  (`frontend/dist` ignored; scratch under `/tmp` only).

## Behavior changes on update (intended, not breaks)

- A task mid-crash-loop (the incident's 10,776-restart state) stops
  crash-looping on first post-update failure: it records a `failed` completion
  and parks after three same-signature strikes instead of spinning.
- Transient git faults now interrupt **with** a human-readable reason
  (same interrupt call, reason string was already supported).
- Mixed-fleet nuance (fail-open): a non-git failure report clears the streak,
  so interleaved old-runner reports delay parking but can never cause a
  wrong park. Worst case is a few extra retries, never a stuck or crashed
  install.

No install-breaking issue found; nothing to fail.

2|# PR Review: Surface runner commit/hook failures in the task UI

10|## Goal 1 — Runner captures structured failure detail: PROVEN

13|  `parseHookFailure` + `buildGitFailureDetails` contract. `readGitSubcommand` correctly skips `-c`
14|  pairs, so the incident's recovery commit (`-c user.name=… -c user.email=… commit -m …`) parses as
15|  `commit` and yields code `git-hook-rejected` with the envelope; hook-less commits keep `git-failed`
16|  and gain `exitCode` + envelope. `merge --abort` stays plain.
17|- All commit sites covered: recovery commit (`refreshWorktreeToRemote`, phase `recovery`),
18|  stage-end `commitAndPush` incl. docs-repo relabel and `integrateUpstream` sync-conflict
19|  (phase `stage-commit`), merge path (`executeIntegrationAssignment`, phase `merge`), eviction/reap
20|  paths (loud `logger.error`, still degrade to `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED`, never crash).
21|- Direct proof (this session, real module, incident-shaped stderr): kind `hook-rejected`,
22|  hook `pre-commit`, exit 1, files `[a.png, b.png, c.png]`-equivalent, full hook output preserved,
23|  concrete re-capture remedy, one-line summary. Real-git incident-replay tests pass:
24|  `runner/daemon.test.js` "reports a hook-rejected recovery commit as a failed completion instead
25|  of crashing" (3 corrupt PNGs, `complete-failed`, 0 interrupts, no throw), stage-commit variant,
26|  merge-commit variant, and the loop-dead test (N failures → N reports, 0 exits, 0 reason-less
27|  interrupts) plus one-poll-cycle backoff.
28|
29|## Goal 2 — Backend records the failure (no stale error): PROVEN
30|
31|- `complete({ outcome: "failed", failureKind: "commit-failed", gitFailure })` is the vehicle.
32|  Route sanitizes via `sanitizeGitFailure` (redact + caps, malformed → warn-and-drop, never 400);
33|  `applyRunnerReport` attaches `err.gitDiagnostics` and leads `err.stdout` with hook output, so the

35|  `[ERROR]` log, `-failure-` report, and `process:exit` with no further changes.

44|  report, `process:exit` carry hook detail) and pin old-runner compat and malformed-payload

47|## Goal 3 — UI renders commit/hook failures clearly: PROVEN (with one evidence gap)
48|
49|- `GitFailureDetails.jsx` (title, mono command + exit + phase, affected-files list, remedy,
50|  capped hook output with Show full output/less) mounts under `FailureMessage` in both
51|  `TaskDetailPageContent.jsx` and `TaskDetailsTabContent.jsx`; banner heading switches to
52|  "⚠️ Commit Failed" via the shared `pickFailureBannerTitle`; `TaskCard.jsx` gets a distinct
53|  "⚠️ Commit Failed" label; timeline rows show the hook file list (`HistoryFailureReason`).

55|  plain-text rendering — pinned by "keeps the generic banner" tests in both views.
56|- Evidence gap: no pixel screenshot — `capture:screenshot` found nothing served on `:3100`
57|  (blank capture, removed) and this review spawns no servers per guidance. Substitution: the
58|  committed render tests drive both banners + card with incident payloads (titles, files, remedy,
59|  expand/collapse, malformed-degradation, stale-expanded-state reset) and pass. Recommend a
60|  staging smoke screenshot post-merge (plan Step 30, still open).
61|
62|## Plan compliance, standards, debt, docs
63|
64|- Follows `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` phases, including incident-replay-first, contract-first,
65|  never-bypass (grep-guard test passes; zero `--no-verify` in `runner/`), and wire-compat rules.

3|

6|installs on update? If yes, fail the stage; do not fix. Read-only audit of
7|`origin/main` (`64e428e6`) vs this branch's HEAD (`5d118739`), plus a live
8|old-install/new-format simulation. Docs-only: this file is the only change.
9|
10|## Verdict: PASS — no install-breaking change found
11|
12|Every persistence, wire, dispatch, and module-loading surface the change
13|touches is additive with a tolerant fallback on both sides of the version
14|skew. The change needs no migration, no new dependency, no new config, and
15|no new task status. Existing tasks on update behave byte-for-byte as before
16|until they newly emit a deterministic git failure — the only update-time
17|behavior change, and it is the feature itself.
18|
19|## Evidence
20|
21|### 1. On-disk format: optional frontmatter line, no migration
22|
23|- `api/work/taskPersistence.js` persists `gitFailureStreak` only when truthy,
24|  via `_formatFrontmatterValue(JSON.stringify(...))` — the exact pattern
25|  already on `main` for `reviewBaseline`, `reportMetadata`, `timelineMetadata`,
26|  etc. (`git show origin/main:...` lines 75/96-98).
27|- `api/work/taskFiles.js` is byte-identical between `origin/main` and HEAD
28|  (verified in the simulation below), and its `_parseFrontmatter` is a generic
29|  `key: value` map. `parseTaskMarkdown` reads only known keys; `gitFailureStreak`
30|  appears 0 times in the `main` version, so older code ignores the line.
31|- Live simulation (`node /tmp/kb_upgrade_sim.mjs`, result archived below):
32|  NEW `saveTaskMarkdown` wrote
33|  `gitFailureStreak: "{\"stageId\":\"build\",...}"` (properly escaped);
34|  the `main` parser bytes read it as an opaque string key; NEW
35|  `parseTaskMarkdown` round-tripped it exactly; tasks without a streak write
36|  no line and parse to `undefined`. Downgrade- and upgrade-safe both ways.
37|- Complementary stale-file tolerance: the new parser drops corrupt streak
38|  JSON silently (fail-open, task dispatches normally), pinned by
39|  `taskPersistence.test.js` ("omits the streak line when absent and tolerates
40|  corrupt values").
41|
42|### 2. Wire contract: additive optional field, tolerated on both sides
43|
44|- Runner → backend: `gitFailure` on `POST /tasks/:id/complete-execution` is
45|  additive. The old handler (`origin/main` `runnerRoutes.js`, inspected) reads
46|  only named `request.body` fields with no JSON-schema validator, so a new
47|  runner talking to an old backend never 400s — the field is ignored and the
48|  failure is still recorded with the one-line `failureReason` (strictly more
49|  visible than today's journal-only behavior, no crash: the daemon catches
50|  report failures and falls back to interrupt-with-reason, then returns).
51|- Backend robustness: `sanitizeGitFailure` drops absent/malformed payloads with
52|  a warning, never a 400, and treats unknown fields leniently. Old-runner
53|  payloads hit the identical code path as before. Pinned by
54|  `applyRunnerReport.test.js` ("old-runner compat"), `runnerRoutes.test.js`,
55|  and `sanitizeGitFailure.test.js`.
56|- `interrupt` gaining an optional `reason` uses a parameter that already
57|  existed on `main` (`executionLedger.interruptExecution` accepts `reason`);
58|  `interrupt()` deliberately still never touches `lastError`.
59|
60|### 3. Dispatch: gate is unreachable for legacy tasks
61|
62|- `isSchedulerRunnable` gains `isGitFailureParked(task)`, which returns `false`
63|  for any task lacking a valid `gitFailureStreak` — i.e. every task in every
64|  existing install on the first post-update dispatch cycle. Parking requires
65|  three NEW successful `complete({outcome:"failed", gitFailure})` reports on
66|  the same stage with the same signature, a state pre-update code cannot
67|  produce.
68|- All four dispatch call sites (`scanClaimableTasks`, `findNextCandidateTask`,
69|  `findResumedCandidate`, `isWaitingForPickup`) go through the single gate, and
70|  the direct-claim `409 GIT_FAILURE_PARKED` follows the established 409-skip
71|  pattern (`RUNNER_VERSION_BELOW_MINIMUM`, `STALE_EPOCH`, …). Operator unpark
72|  paths (retry / resume / move / success advance) all clear the streak
73|  (`stageTransitions.js`).
74|- Embedded (non-runner) dispatch shares the gate but can never create a
75|  streak — identical behavior for embedded installs.
76|
77|### 4. Classification: new tag only, old heuristics untouched
78|
79|- `classifyStageError` gains one early equality branch for
80|  `failureKind === "commit-failed"` → `logical/commit-failed` (failback,
81|  non-retryable). The abort/auth/infra checks it precedes are untouched; the
82|  `"infrastructure"` tag check and every other classifier branch are unchanged.
83|  Old runners never send `"commit-failed"`, so no pre-existing report changes
84|  classification after update.
85|- `circuitSensors` likewise only adds `commit-failed` exclusions; all other
86|  kinds take the identical path.
87|- `failureKind` is a new value in an existing string field — no schema change,
88|  no new status, no exhaustive switch anywhere (`=== "rejected"`,
89|  `=== "infrastructure"` checks tolerate it by falling through).
90|
91|### 5. Module loading and packaging: no new dependency, existing layouts
92|
93|- `shared/gitFailure.js` (re-export shim) + `shared/gitFailure/` are importable
94|  everywhere required: `origin/main` `runner/daemon.js` already imports four
95|  `../shared/*.js` modules, so every runner install ships `shared/`;
96|  dozens of frontend files already import `../../../../shared/*.js` and
97|  `frontend/vite.config.js` sets `server.fs.allow: ['..']`.
98|- Live proof: `node --check` on all new files; ESM import smoke of
99|  `shared/gitFailure.js` (all 9 exports resolve); `npm run build --prefix
100|  frontend` succeeds (the new `GitFailureDetails.jsx` import bundles).
101|- `git diff --name-only` shows no `package.json`, lockfile, manifest, or env
102|  change. The pre-commit hook change is a 2-line comment. No new runner test
103|  files were added, so no `run-tests.mjs` registration was needed.
104|
105|### 6. Frontend old/new skew
106|
107|- Old frontend + new backend: `isRejectedTask` is `=== "rejected"`, so
108|  `failureKind: "commit-failed"` renders the generic banner; `gitDiagnostics`
109|  rides the untouched `gitDiagnosticsOf` channel (byte-identical file on both
110|  sides) and is ignored by old renders. No crash path.
111|- New frontend + old payloads: `GitFailureDetails` is null-safe on
112|  absent/malformed diagnostics and `isCommitFailureTask` is shape-gated
113|  (`hookOutput` string + `files` array + `remedy` string), so backend
114|  `merge-conflict`/`sync-blocked` shapes and plain failures keep the exact
115|  old banner — pinned in both `TaskDetailPage.test.jsx` and
116|  `TaskDetailsTabContent.test.jsx`.
117|
118|## Test evidence (this session)
119|
120|- Backend touched set via the project entry (`npm run test:api -- …`):
121|  349/349 pass (12 files, incl. streak round-trip, old-runner compat,
122|  malformed-payload, parking, scheduler gate, taxonomy, circuit sensors).
123|  Note: invoking `api/node_modules/.bin/vitest` from the repo root
124|  mis-resolved the config and produced 11 environment-only failures in
125|  `circuitSensors.test.js` / `taskErrors.taxonomy.test.js`; the same files
126|  pass via the project entry. Not a code issue.
127|- Frontend touched set (`npm run test:frontend -- …`): 154/154 pass (6 files).
128|- Runner touched set (`node --test runner/…`): 246/246 pass (4 files).
129|- Upgrade simulation (`node /tmp/kb_upgrade_sim.mjs`): taskFiles
130|  byte-identical; newline-free escaped streak line; old parser surface reads
131|  it as an opaque key (`main` has 0 references); new parser round-trips;
132|  streakless tasks parse to `undefined`. `git status` clean afterwards
133|  (`frontend/dist` ignored; scratch under `/tmp` only).
134|
135|## Behavior changes on update (intended, not breaks)
136|
137|- A task mid-crash-loop (the incident's 10,776-restart state) stops
138|  crash-looping on first post-update failure: it records a `failed` completion
139|  and parks after three same-signature strikes instead of spinning.
140|- Transient git faults now interrupt **with** a human-readable reason
141|  (same interrupt call, reason string was already supported).
142|- Mixed-fleet nuance (fail-open): a non-git failure report clears the streak,
143|  so interleaved old-runner reports delay parking but can never cause a
144|  wrong park. Worst case is a few extra retries, never a stuck or crashed
145|  install.
146|
147|No install-breaking issue found; nothing to fail.
